name: Martin Ward

bio.statement: Ward's voters' pamphlet statement lists a master's degree in political science.
Ward's city filing form lists his current occupation as not employed.

source.publisher: City of Portland Auditor's Office, Elections

bio.statement: The Portland Mercury describes Ward as a perennial candidate in Oregon politics.
bio.excerpt: Ward, 35, is a professional and perennial candidate in Oregon politics.

positions.statement: Ward's voters' pamphlet statement proposes an estimated $1-1.5 billion in budget cuts, mainly by cutting construction projects.
positions.excerpt: Have an estimated 1-1.5 billion dollars of budget cuts, mainly by cutting construction projects

positions.statement: Ward's pamphlet statement says government ownership has lowered rent by around 30-40% by eliminating landlords.
positions.excerpt: Government ownership has shown to lower rent by around 30-40% due to the elimination of landlords

positions.statement: Ward's pamphlet statement says about $600 million is needed to build permanent shelters for all homeless people.
positions.excerpt: Need about 600 million to build new permanent shelters to house all homeless

positions.statement: Ward's pamphlet statement says he would fund food stamps at about $20-30 million a year.
positions.excerpt: Will fund food stamps, need about 20-30 million annually.

positions.statement: Ward's pamphlet statement proposes making grades 6-12 more focused on students' desired occupations.
positions.excerpt: Main reforms will revolve around having 6-12th grade be more focused on students' desired occupation.

positions.statement: Ward's pamphlet statement says he would stop the demolition of Lloyd Center and pursue a plan to revitalize the mall.
positions.excerpt: Will stop the demolition of lloyd center, and roll out a more reasonable plan to revitalize the mall.

positions.statement: OPB reports Ward wants to cut city construction projects and install more surveillance cameras to address crime.
positions.excerpt: Martin Ward, unemployed, wants to cut city construction projects and install more surveillance cameras to address crime.

positions.statement: The Portland Mercury reports Ward plans to eliminate almost every local tax and fee.
positions.excerpt: plans to eliminate almost every local tax and fee

gaps: No voting record (has not held elected office)

collection_notes: Steps run identically for all 21 District 3 candidates: (1) county Military & Overseas Online Voters' Guide statement PDF (with the full and large-print county pamphlets tried where the statement PDF was a scan; the pamphlet's candidate index marks candidates who filed no statement) plus the City Auditor's AUD-120 candidate filing form linked from portland.gov's 2026 city candidates page; (2) portland.gov/council roster and councilor page for incumbents; (3) campaign domain only as printed in the pamphlet statement or filing form; (4) one general WebSearch; (5) three fixed allowed-domain WebSearch groups (opb.org+oregoncapitalchronicle.com+wweek.com+ballotpedia.org; kgw.com+koin.com+kptv.com+katu.com; portlandmercury.com+vote411.org+pamplinmedia.com+portlandtribune.com) because the search proxy rejects oregonlive.com and apnews.com; (6) the three articles that cover the whole District 3 field: OPB 'What to know about Portland's District 3 council race' (2026-10-07), Portland Mercury 'Meet the Candidates For City Council District 3' (2026-09-09) and Portland Tribune 'Meet the Portland City Council District 3 candidates' (2026-10-13; Q&A — the Tribune says Sollitt, Pham, Parker, McCormick, Kelly and Frankenstein did not respond and Tucker withdrew). Multi-winner race: OPB states three council seats are available in District 3. Excerpts come through a summarizing fetch tool that limits verbatim quotes to ~125 characters, so some are fragments. Ballot name/order match inventory.json and the county Ballot Content RCV report. Ward ran for Portland mayor in 2024 (OPB 2024 profile in search results).
